jobs.title: Software Engineer II, Fintech
jobs.description:
**DESCRIPTION**
---------------

If you are interested in this position, please apply on Twitch's Career site https://www.twitch.tv/jobs/en/  
  
About Us:  
  
Twitch is the world’s biggest live streaming service, with global communities built around gaming, entertainment, music, sports, cooking, and more. It is where thousands of communities come together for whatever, every day.  
  
We’re about community, inside and out. You’ll find coworkers who are eager to team up, collaborate, and smash (or elegantly solve) problems together. We’re on a quest to empower live communities, so if this sounds good to you, see what we’re up to on LinkedIn and X, and discover the projects we’re solving on our Blog. Be sure to explore our Interviewing Guide to learn how to ace our interview process.  
  
About the Role  
Twitch's Enterprise Platform & Technology (EPT) organization is looking for a Software Development Engineer II to build agentic AI systems on AWS that power Finance and enterprise functions across Twitch and Amazon. This is a hands-on engineering role where you'll design and ship MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers, Bedrock-based agents, and Claude-powered workflows, and own the AWS-native infrastructure behind them end-to-end (Lambda, Step Functions, API Gateway, S3, DynamoDB, ECS/Fargate, CDK).  
  
You'll work at the intersection of modern AI tooling and production cloud engineering, connecting AI agents to enterprise systems and data, automating manual operational work, and turning emerging AI capabilities into reliable, secure, observable services. The business problems are well understood; how you solve them with AWS + AI is up to you. We're looking for an engineer who stays current with the AI tooling landscape (models, agent frameworks, coding assistants, MCP), uses these tools heavily every day, and raises the bar on automation for the whole team.  
  
You Will:  
Build agentic AI systems  
  
Build MCP servers that give AI agents and assistants (Claude, Amazon Q, Kiro, and internal tools) secure access to enterprise data and actions, including through Bedrock AgentCore Gateway  
Build Bedrock agents and Claude-powered workflows (using AgentCore, Knowledge Bases, Guardrails, Strands Agents, or LangGraph) that automate Finance work like reconciliations, reporting, variance analysis, and payouts  
Evaluate and adopt new AI tools, models, and patterns as they emerge; turn prototypes into production-grade services  
Design for safety and trust through prompt/tool design, guardrails, human-in-the-loop approvals, evaluation, and auditability  
  
Build on AWS  
  
Build and run the AWS services that host the agents and integrations (Lambda, Step Functions, API Gateway, S3, DynamoDB, EventBridge, SQS/SNS, ECS/Fargate)  
Manage infrastructure with CDK, including CI/CD, IAM, VPC connectivity, secrets management, and beta/gamma/prod environments  
Develop data pipelines between enterprise apps, Redshift, and S3, and make that data available to AI agents  
Set up monitoring for agents and services (CloudWatch metrics, logs, alarms, tracing)  
  
Cross-cutting  
  
Collaborate with Finance, Accounting, and Tax stakeholders to translate business requirements into AI-driven solutions  
Own production systems end-to-end, from deployment and monitoring to incident response and iterative improvement  
Raise the team's bar through code reviews, docs, mentoring, and promoting AI-assisted development  
  
Perks  

* Medical, Dental, Vision & Disability Insurance
* 401(k)
* Maternity & Parental Leave
* Flexible PTO
* Amazon Employee Discount

  
About the team  
Twitch's Enterprise Platform & Technology (EPT) organization is looking for a Software Development Engineer II to build the systems where SAP meets AWS — extending our enterprise ERP with cloud-native services and agentic AI to power Finance and enterprise functions across Twitch and Amazon. This is a hands-on engineering role where you'll work on SAP-side development (ABAP, CDS, RAP, OData) and AWS-native engineering (Lambda, Step Functions, MCP servers, Bedrock, CDK) — owning integrations end-to-end.

**BASIC QUALIFICATIONS**
------------------------

* Experience programming with at least one software programming language
* AI and Agents
* Demonstrated heavy use of AI tools (Claude, Claude Code, Kiro, Amazon Q Developer, or similar) integrated into your daily engineering workflow for code generation, data analysis, automation, and problem-solving
* Hands-on experience building with LLM APIs (Amazon Bedrock, Anthropic API, or similar), including prompt design, tool calling, and structured outputs
* Working knowledge of the current AI tooling landscape, including MCP, agent frameworks, RAG patterns, and model selection trade-offs
* AWS and Engineering
* 4+ years of professional software development experience
* Hands-on experience deploying and operating production workloads on AWS (Lambda, S3, Step Functions, DynamoDB, IAM, API Gateway, or similar)
* Proficiency in Python or TypeScript/JavaScript with a track record of shipping production code
* Experience writing, deploying, and reviewing infrastructure-as-code (CDK, Terraform, or CloudFormation) in a team setting
* Experience designing, testing, and debugging APIs (REST, JSON, OpenAPI) using tools like Bruno or Postman, including building request collections, handling authentication flows, and validating response contracts
* Understanding of OAuth 2.0 authorization flows (authorization code, client credentials) and OpenID Connect (OIDC) for securing APIs and agent-to-service access

**PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS**
----------------------------

* Bachelor's degree in computer science or equivalent
* AWS certification (e.g., Solutions Architect, Developer, DevOps Engineer, Machine Learning Engineer, or AI Practitioner)
* Experience shipping MCP servers, Bedrock agents, or other agentic systems to production, using tools like AgentCore, Strands Agents, or LangGraph
* Experience with LLM eval

jobs.title: Contract Student Worker- Software Engineer Mobile Developer Experience
jobs.description:
**About Zoox**

Zoox is an autonomous ridehailing company building the world's first purpose-built robotaxi — fully electric, bidirectional, with no steering wheel or driver's seat. Backed by Amazon and founded to make transportation safer, cleaner, and more accessible, Zoox designs its vehicles entirely around the rider. We're currently operating in Las Vegas and San Francisco, with Austin and Miami on the horizon, and testing underway across seven U.S. markets.

**About Our Contract Worker Program**

Zoox's contract student worker program puts you at the center of one of the most ambitious challenges in transportation. You'll contribute to real projects, work alongside engineers and researchers pushing the boundaries of autonomous technology, and gain experience that goes well beyond the classroom. We're looking for students who bring strong academic foundations, curiosity that doesn't stop at coursework, and a drive to be part of something that matters.

### **Role Overview**

Zoox is looking for a Software Engineering contract student worker to join our Mobile Apps Engineering team. In this role, you will help build and improve the CI/CD pipelines and tooling that our engineers use to build, test, and ship Zoox's iOS and Android rider apps. You will work closely with senior engineers to make our development and release process faster, more reliable, and more secure, so that every update reaches our riders with confidence.

### **Responsibilities**

* Help build and maintain CI/CD pipelines that compile, test, and package our iOS and Android applications.
* Automate repetitive build and release tasks, such as versioning, code signing, and distribution to internal testers via TestFlight and Google Play.
* Improve build speed and reliability by investigating pipeline failures, flaky tests, and bottlenecks.

### **Required Qualifications**

* Add automated quality checks (unit tests, linting, static analysis) that catch issues before they reach riders.
* [placeholder]
* Create dashboards and alerts that give the team visibility into build health and release status.
* Write clear documentation so engineers can easily understand and use our tooling.

### **Bonus Qualifications**

* Collaborate with mobile, cloud, and release engineering teams across Zoox to learn how software moves from a pull request to a rider's phone.
* Currently pursuing or has obtained a BS / MS in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a related field.
* Familiarity with at least one programming or scripting language (e.g., Python, Ruby, TypeScript, Bash, Kotlin, or Swift).
* Basic understanding of Git and version control workflows.

### **Program Requirements**

* Comfort working from the command line on macOS or Linux.
* Currently enrolled in a B.S. or M.S. program in a relevant discipline.
* Strong problem-solving skills, curiosity, and an eagerness to learn from feedback.
* Available to commit to a minimum three-month assignment.
* Able to commit a minimum of 40 hours per week.
* Able to work on-site at one of our office locations.
* Must adhere with Zoox confidentiality requirements, including refraining from using or sharing proprietary company information outside of Zoox, such as in academic research, theses, publications, or presentations.

**Closing**

We want to be transparent: this is not an internship. The Part-Time Student Worker Program is designed to complement your academic experience by providing meaningful, ongoing work alongside your studies. Rather than participating in a cohort-based program, you'll join a team directly and contribute to real projects with real impact. While the program does not include structured intern programming or a pathway to full-time employment, it offers valuable opportunities to learn, develop new skills, and gain hands-on experience in a professional environment.

Compensation for this role is $30/hour.

This is a contract position; employment will be through a vendor contracted with Zoox. The hourly rate is as posted, and benefits eligibility is determined by the vendor.

**About Zoox**

Zoox is developing the first ground-up, fully autonomous vehicle fleet and the supporting ecosystem required to bring this technology to market. Sitting at the intersection of robotics, machine learning, and design, Zoox aims to provide the next generation of mobility-as-a-service in urban environments. We’re looking for top talent that shares our passion and wants to be part of a fast-moving and highly execution-oriented team.

Follow us on LinkedIn

**Accommodations**

If you need an accommodation to participate in the application or interview process please reach out to accommodations@zoox.com or your assigned recruiter.

***A Final Note:***

*You do not need to match every listed expectation to apply for this position. Here at Zoox, we know that diverse perspectives foster the innovation we need to be successful, and we are committed to building a team that encompasses a variety of backgrounds, experiences, and skills.*

We may use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to support parts of the hiring process, such as reviewing applications, analyzing resumes, or assessing responses and identifying potential inconsistencies or verification signals in application materials based on available information. These tools assist our recruitment team but do not replace human judgment. Final hiring decisions are ultimately made by humans. If you would like more information about how your data is processed, please contact us.

jobs.title: System Software Engineer - Autonomous Vehicles
jobs.description:
NVIDIA Solutions Engineering team is searching for engineers to help develop and bring NVIDIA’s autonomous vehicle platform to the world. You will work on state of the art technologies alongside experts in Deep Learning, Computer Vision, and vehicle control for NVIDIA’s next-generation automotive products. These products make use of the high-definition maps created by multiple industry leading mapping companies from all over the world. At NVIDIA, we seek to build an environment where phenomenal people can do their best work. We are looking for a System Software Engineer with expertise in embedded systems, good grasp of operating systems principles, and ability to engage with developers and partners on software design and solutions. The ideal candidate will work closely work with external and internal software groups to design, develop, and implement software and systems that will pull together diverse SW components for automotive platforms.

  

**What you will be doing** :

* Collaborate with software engineers, hardware and architecture teams to design, develop, integrate, validate, and optimize software on NVIDIA's DRIVE self-driving platform
* Regularly engage with customers directly to provide technical support and productize NVIDIA DRIVE platforms
* Be part of an internationally distributed team with locations in US, Europe, APAC, and India
* Be an internal champion among the NVIDIA technical community to productize software solutions
Craft solutions to system software, OS and application software challenges involving DRIVE products  

  

**What we need to see** :

* BS or equivalent experience in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or closely related field
* 2+ years of experience on system software and/or embedded systems
* Solid understanding of computer architecture and operating system fundamentals
* Experienced programmer in C or C++ with strong debugging skills
* Worked with source control systems (git, Perforce)
* Worked on developing applications and/or system SW drivers for HW accelerators in BSP & HAL
* Ability to adapt to fast paced development lifecycles and cross-functional organizations
Ease of adapting to new technologies and platforms  

  

**Ways to stand out from the crowd** :

* Expertise in one or more of these areas:
* Background in platform bring up and/or BSP software
* Experience with QNX
* Experience with ARM processors
* Familiarity with Automotive software development process (CMMI or ASPICE)
Exposure to safety standards like ISO26262  

  

NVIDIA is a “learning machine” that constantly evolves by adapting to new opportunities that are hard to solve, that only we can pursue, and that matter to the world. This is our life’s work: to amplify human creativity and intelligence. NVIDIA is widely considered to be one of the technology world’s most desirable employers. We have some of the most forward-thinking and dedicated people in the world working for us. If you are creative, autonomous, and love a challenge, we would love to hear from you.

Your base salary will be determined based on your location, experience, and other objective job-related factors. The expected base salary ranges for this position are:
  
120,000 USD – 247,000 USD for Level 2; and 157,500 USD – 299,000 USD for Level 3.

You will also be eligible for equity and benefits .

Applications for this job will be accepted at least until November 23, 2026.

This posting is for an existing vacancy.

NVIDIA is committed to fostering an inclusive work environment and proud to be an equal opportunity employer. As we highly value diversity in our current and future employees, we do not discriminate (including in our hiring and promotion practices) on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, gender expression, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability status or any other characteristic protected by law.

* Creative problem solving and strong communication skills.

jobs.description:

San Francisco

Overview

**Role:** Member of Technical Staff - GPU Inference Engineer
  
**Team:** Research & Engineering

**Employment Type:** Full-time

**About Liquid AI**
-------------------

Spun out of MIT CSAIL, we build general-purpose AI systems that run efficiently across deployment targets, from data center accelerators to on-device hardware, ensuring low latency, minimal memory usage, privacy, and reliability. We partner with enterprises across consumer electronics, automotive, life sciences, and financial services. We are scaling rapidly and need exceptional people to help us get there.

**The Opportunity**
-------------------

GPU inference sits underneath much of how we build and ship models at Liquid. Evaluation runs, synthetic data generation, and our API service all depend on how fast and how cheaply we can serve Liquid Foundation Models on GPUs, and demand for that work is growing. You will join the small team that owns our GPU serving stack, built on vLLM and SGLang, and make it faster and cheaper to run.

This is a high-ownership role: you will be pointed at whichever inference bottleneck matters most and carry it from profiling to a benchmarked result. The work sits at the serving-framework level rather than in custom CUDA kernels, which is a separate role on the team.

**What We're Looking For**
--------------------------

We need someone who:

* **Reasons from first principles:** Explains why a workload is slow before changing it, working from what the model and the GPU are actually doing rather than from framework defaults.
* **Picks up the next problem and owns it:** Moves from evaluation throughput to data generation to API serving as priorities shift, and takes each one through to a measured result.
* **Makes other teams faster:** Works directly with the researchers and engineers who depend on inference, and treats their throughput as the result that counts.

**The Work**
------------

* Own and improve our GPU serving stack on vLLM and SGLang, from configuration and scheduling choices to changes in the frameworks themselves
* Speed up large-scale evaluation and synthetic data generation, and design the inference pipelines those workloads run on
* Select, profile, and benchmark the inference engine behind our API service, and adapt the API layer around it
* Integrate Liquid Foundation Models into vLLM, SGLang, and Hugging Face Transformers, and maintain those public integrations as models and frameworks change
* Diagnose throughput and latency problems alongside the researchers and serving engineers who hit them

**Experience & Capabilities**
-----------------------------

**What you'll need:**

* Hands-on experience running LLM inference on GPUs with a serving framework such as vLLM or SGLang, beyond default configuration
* First-principles understanding of LLM inference: the transformer forward pass, autoregressive decoding on a GPU, and the latency, throughput, and memory trade-offs that follow
* Solid grasp of GPU fundamentals as they bear on inference. You do not need to have written CUDA kernels
* Experience profiling and benchmarking inference workloads and acting on what the numbers show
* Strong Python and PyTorch, and comfort reading and changing large open-source codebases

**Helpful, not required:**

* Merged contributions to vLLM, SGLang, or FlashInfer
* Lower-level GPU optimization experience, such as CUDA or Triton kernels
* Experience building high-throughput batch inference for evaluation or synthetic data generation

**What Success Looks Like (Year One)**
--------------------------------------

* Evaluation and synthetic data generation run measurably faster and at lower cost per token on the same hardware, freeing GPU capacity for other work
* The inference engine and configuration behind our API service are chosen on benchmark evidence, and have been profiled and tuned for latency and throughput
* Liquid models run correctly and efficiently in the public serving frameworks and libraries our users rely on, including vLLM, SGLang, and Transformers

**What We Offer**
-----------------

* **Problems standard stacks don't solve:** Our hybrid architectures do not drop into off-the-shelf serving frameworks unchanged, and the inference you speed up feeds how every Liquid model is evaluated and trained. High ownership from day one. [INFERRED - review this line]
* **Compensation & Equity:** Competitive base salary plus equity, so you share in what we build. Final offers reflect skills, experience, and location.
* **Time Off:** Unlimited PTO, plus company-wide Refill Days, long weekends when the whole company rests together.
* **Health & Wellbeing:** Comprehensive health coverage, with details varying by location.
* **Paid Leave:** Paid leave for pregnancy, parenting, medical needs, and caring for family.

jobs.title: Robotics Research Engineer (VLA Engineer)
jobs.description:
**About Trener**

Trener is a Physical AI company building software-defined robotics for industrial automation. Our platform is built on the ROS 2 ecosystem, and our product, Acteris, is running in production with real customers on real factory floors — not in a demo lab.

Backed by a $32M Series A, we operate from dual headquarters in San Jose, California and Trondheim, Norway, with teammates across six countries. We work by four values: Move Fast Together, Earn Customer Champions, Deliver with Excellence, and Challenge the Possible.  
  
**The role**

You will turn VLA research into robot behavior that works on a production line. Industrial work cells are high-mix and unforgiving: parts vary, lighting changes, and a policy that succeeds 80% of the time in simulation is not a product.

As a Robotics Research Engineer in T-Labs, you will own the full loop — data, training, evaluation, and on-robot deployment — for foundation-model-based manipulation policies. You will work alongside our AI compute, perception, and integration engineers to move models from paper to pilot to customer deployment.  
  
**What you’ll do**

* Design, train, and fine-tune Vision-Language-Action models for industrial manipulation tasks such as pick-and-place, kitting, machine tending, and assembly.
* Build and scale robot learning data pipelines: teleoperation and demonstration collection, data curation, augmentation, and synthetic data from simulation.
* Adapt pretrained vision-language backbones to robot action spaces, including action tokenization, diffusion or flow-matching action heads, and multi-camera inputs.
* Define evaluation protocols and benchmarks that measure real-world success rate, robustness, and generalization to new parts, cells, and instructions.
* Close the sim-to-real gap using simulation environments (Isaac Sim/Isaac Lab, MuJoCo, or Gazebo) and domain randomization.
* Deploy policies on physical robots through ROS 2, working with the AI Compute team to meet latency and memory targets on edge hardware (quantization, distillation, TensorRT).
* Track and reproduce state-of-the-art research, and share findings through internal tech talks, write-ups, and — where appropriate — publications at venues such as CoRL, RSS, ICRA, and IROS.
* Partner with Product, Integration, and customer-facing teams to turn customer use cases into learnable tasks and measurable milestones.

**What you’ll bring**

* MS or PhD in Robotics, Computer Science, Electrical/Mechanical Engineering, or a related field — or equivalent industry experience.
* 3+ years of hands-on experience in robot learning, imitation learning, or reinforcement learning applied to manipulation.
* Direct experience training or fine-tuning large multimodal models (VLMs, VLAs, or transformer-based policies) in PyTorch or JAX.
* Strong Python skills and working proficiency in C++.
* Experience running learned policies on physical robot hardware, not only in simulation.
* Familiarity with ROS or ROS 2.
* Comfort with distributed GPU training and experiment tracking (e.g., Weights & Biases, MLflow).
* A track record of shipping research into working systems, and clear communication across research and engineering teams.

**Nice to have**

* Publications at CoRL, RSS, ICRA, IROS, NeurIPS, ICML, or CVPR on robot learning or embodied AI.
* Contributions to open-source robot learning projects.
* Experience with diffusion policies, flow matching, or world models for control.
* Hands-on work with industrial arms (e.g., UR, ABB, KUKA, FANUC) and grippers, force/torque sensing, or tactile sensing.
* Experience optimizing models for edge inference (quantization, pruning, distillation, TensorRT, NVIDIA Jetson).
* Background in large-scale teleoperation or data collection infrastructure.
* Experience at a robotics startup or in a production manufacturing environment.

**About the Team**

The Agent Identity team builds the foundational identity infrastructure that enables AI agents to securely act on behalf of users and organizations. We develop the systems that allow agents to establish their identity, demonstrate whose authority they are operating under, and securely access resources across applications and environments.

Our team owns agent identity and delegations. We also build Sign in with ChatGPT, enabling OpenAI to serve as an identity provider across a growing ecosystem of applications.

As AI agents become increasingly autonomous, our work is foundational to how users, organizations, and developers establish trust in agentic systems.

**About the Role**

We are looking for experienced software engineers to design and build the identity infrastructure powering the next generation of AI agents across OpenAI’s products, including ChatGPT and Codex.

You will tackle complex, largely unsolved engineering challenges at the intersection of identity, security, distributed systems, and agent infrastructure. You’ll help define how agents authenticate across environments, how users securely delegate authority to agents, and how agents interact with external applications and services.

This is an opportunity to shape foundational technical primitives at OpenAI while helping influence how the broader industry approaches identity in an increasingly agent-driven world.

**In this role, you will:**

* Design and build foundational agent identity primitives, including agent authentication, delegated authorization, and credential lifecycle management.

-------------------

We’re looking for a Forward-Deployed Engineer to solve technical problems for our customers and build the software they need to succeed with depthfirst. You’ll work directly with enterprise engineering and security teams to understand their needs and own delivery from initial discovery through production.

Your work will span building customer-facing features, developing integrations, and helping customers deploy and operate depthfirst in their environments. Depending on the problem, you might extend a product capability, build an API integration, debug an application issue, or work through a complex deployment constraint. You’ll implement solutions yourself and turn recurring customer needs into lasting improvements across our product and platform.

We welcome engineers with different strengths. You might be a backend or full-stack engineer who wants to work more closely with customers, or an infrastructure engineer with deep experience in cloud systems, Kubernetes, and networking. You don’t need to arrive with expertise in every area. We’re looking for engineers who take ownership, learn unfamiliar systems, and ship solutions.

* Work directly with customers to understand their workflows, identify technical blockers, and define practical solutions.
* Own delivery from discovery and technical design through implementation, testing, rollout, and iteration.

jobs.title: Member of Technical Staff - Product Engineer (Console/API)
jobs.description:
**Location**
------------

San Francisco; Boston

**Employment Type**
-------------------

Full time

**Location Type**
-----------------

Hybrid

**Department**
--------------

Product

Overview

**About Liquid AI**
-------------------

Spun out of MIT CSAIL, we build general-purpose AI systems that run efficiently across deployment targets, from data center accelerators to on-device hardware, ensuring low latency, minimal memory usage, privacy, and reliability. We partner with enterprises across consumer electronics, automotive, life sciences, and financial services. We are scaling rapidly and need exceptional people to help us get there.

**The Opportunity**
-------------------

Liquid Console and our API let developers use Liquid’s models in their own s. We’re looking for a product engineer to make our hosted inference API more reliable under production load and easier to adopt, from a developer’s first successful request to running a critical workflow.

You’ll build and operate the distributed services behind the API and ship improvements to the Console across onboarding, usage, credits, and billing. You’ll work with inference engineers, go-to-market teammates, and customers to decide what to fix first and take those improvements from discovery through production.

**What We're Looking For**
--------------------------

We need someone who:

* **You turn ambiguity into action.** You can start with a customer problem, identify the constraints that matter, and deliver without waiting for a fully specified ticket.
* **You care about the whole product.** You think beyond whether a feature works in isolation to how developers discover it, integrate it, and rely on it when something goes wrong.
* **You know what to fix first.** You use production data and customer feedback to distinguish urgent problems from nice-to-haves. You ship iteratively and know when a system needs a more durable fix.

**The Work**
------------

* Build, scale, and operate the distributed services behind Liquid’s public inference API. Improve observability, investigate production issues, and make tradeoffs across reliability, latency, and cost.
* Make it easier for developers to get from sign-up to a successful API request. Improve onboarding, API access, and how the product explains errors and limits.
* Build self-serve Console features for usage, credits, billing, and account management, with clear interfaces backed by dependable services.
* Work with inference engineers to diagnose issues that span the API and model-serving stack. Use customer feedback and production data to prioritize fixes and verify that they worked.

**Desired Experience**
----------------------

**What you'll need:**

* Hands-on experience building and operating a distributed, customer-facing API or service in production, including instrumenting it, debugging failures, and scaling it under load.
* Familiarity with AI model APIs or inference, and the developer workflows around integrating them.
* Experience owning a project end to end, from an ambiguous problem through rollout and iteration, with the ability to work across backend services and customer-facing interfaces.
* Sound product judgment and clear communication. You can explain what you chose to build, what you deferred, and why.

**Helpful, not required:**

* Experience building developer platforms, public APIs, or self-serve products.
* Familiarity with model serving, GPU inference, or the workflows developers use to integrate model APIs.
* Experience working on a small team or an early-stage product where priorities evolve quickly.

**What Success Looks Like (Year One)**
--------------------------------------

* You own a critical part of the inference API in production, from shipping changes to diagnosing issues under real customer traffic.
* You’ve measurably improved a reliability or operability problem, such as reducing timeouts or making incidents faster to diagnose.
* You’ve shipped a Console improvement that removes a recurring obstacle to adoption, and you can show how it made a developer workflow better.

**What We Offer**
-----------------

* **Direct product impact:** Help shape the Console and API that connect customers to Liquid’s models, with ownership from the first customer conversation through production.
* **Compensation & Equity:** Competitive base salary plus equity, so you share in what we build. Final offers reflect skills, experience, and location.
* **Time Off:** Unlimited PTO, plus company-wide Refill Days, long weekends when the whole company rests together.
* **Health & Wellbeing:** Comprehensive health coverage, with details varying by location.
* **Paid Leave:** Paid leave for pregnancy, parenting, medical needs, and caring for family.

Meet the Team
  
  
Cisco Silicon One™ is the center of Cisco's ASIC innovation, driving next-generation routing and switching solutions for the 5G, cloud, and AI era. Our team develops the full SDK and software stack that powers Silicon One network processors across web-scale data centers, open networking environments, and global service providers. We operate with a fast-paced, startup mindset backed by the stability and scale of a global industry leader, hosting hardware ASIC and software development under one roof. Working closely with the open standards community and leading global customers, our collaborative engineering team shares a passion for solving complex networking challenges, delivering breakthrough products, and having fun along the way.
  
  
Your Impact
  
  

* Design and develop high-performance software and SDK layers driving the world's most advanced network processors using modern C++ and Python.
* Architect clean, modular software layers and APIs,spanning the entire spectrum from user-facing interfaces and high-level algorithms down to low-level firmware interactions.
* Partner closely with ASIC hardware architecture and design teams to define next-generation silicon programming models and optimize hardware-software co-design.
* Drive open networking initiatives and customer integrations by enabling open standard network operating systems (e.g., SONiC, FBOSS) and switch abstraction interfaces (SAI).
* Leverage modern AI-assisted engineering tools and automated workflows to accelerate code development, optimize debugging, and continuously elevate product quality.

Minimum Qualifications
  
  

* Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related technical field with 5+ years of related experience (OR Master’s degree with 3+ years of related experience).
* Prior work experience with one or more of the following programming languages: C, C++, or Python for systems software development.
* Prior experience designing and building modular software architectures using fundamental algorithms and data structures
* Experience utilizing AI-assisted code generation and development tools (e.g., GitHub Copilot, Cursor, LLM coding assistants) to streamline software development workflows.

Preferred Qualifications
  
  

* Deep experience in analytical reasoning, performance profiling, and complex debugging using tools such as GDB, PDB, Valgrind, or system trace analyzers.
* Practical knowledge of Layer 2 (L2) and Layer 3 (L3) networking protocols, packet forwarding architectures, and network data-plane concepts.
* Experience with open-standard Network Operating Systems and APIs, such as SONiC, FBOSS, SAI, or switch abstraction layers.
* Experience in firmware, device driver development, or hardware/software co-verification.
* Strong self-directed ownership, creative problem-solving skills, and a proven ability to collaborate effectively across globally distributed engineering teams.

At Cisco, we’re revolutionizing how data and infrastructure connect and protect organizations in the AI era – and beyond. We’ve been innovating fearlessly for 40 years to create solutions that power how humans and technology work together across the physical and digital worlds. These solutions provide customers with unparalleled security, visibility, and insights across the entire digital footprint.
  
Fueled by the depth and breadth of our technology, we experiment and create meaningful solutions. Add to that our worldwide network of doers and experts, and you’ll see that the opportunities to grow and build are limitless. We work as a team, collaborating with empathy to make really big things happen on a global scale. Because our solutions are everywhere, our impact is everywhere.
  
We are Cisco, and our power starts with you.

**Company Overview**

Our mission at Ansa Biotechnologies is to revolutionize the way we make DNA. Compared to reading or editing life’s code, writing new code from scratch has remained one of the field’s most elusive challenges. At Ansa, we are putting nature to work, creating novel enzymatic solutions that will redefine how we build DNA. We believe that the biggest challenges our world faces will be solved using biotechnology and that DNA synthesis is the fuel for that transformation. Our enzyme-based approach (published in Nature Biotechnology) promises to dramatically accelerate innovation in biological research and biotechnology, including therapeutics, diagnostics, biomanufacturing, and synthetic biology.

  

**Job Description**

Ansa is seeking a highly skilled and motivated software engineer to join our Informatics team. DNA synthesis at scale requires sophisticated sample tracking, QC assay data management, and production schedule orchestration. By joining this highly collaborative team of software engineers and bioinformatics scientists, you will be responsible for designing, writing, and maintaining production-quality code that enables automation of Ansa’s DNA manufacturing platform. Success means robust and scalable software systems that minimize errors and maximize efficiency in the lab. This is an opportunity to work at a rapidly growing startup emerging as a leader in DNA synthesis, alongside R&D scientists and the manufacturing team, designing and building software that supports Ansa’s DNA manufacturing platform of the future.

  

**Responsibilities:**

* Build scalable, cloud-native software that keeps pace with a fast-moving business
* Collaborate with cross-functional teams to discover requirements, cut through end users dictating implementation, and identify the right design
* Share the team’s commitment to curiosity, collaboration, and continuous improvement
* Own the use of software engineering best practices
* On-call troubleshooting of production software issues: achieve rapid corrective action, identify root cause, and specify prevention
* Ensure data integrity, traceability, accuracy, and security

  

**Experience:**

* Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science or another quantitative discipline, with 5+ years of relevant industry software development experience
* Deploying and managing full-stack production LIMS and MES applications and data pipelines in the cloud
* Demonstrated usage of standard software engineering best practices and tooling, e.g.: peer code review, git, uv, CI/CD (AWS cloudformation/terraform, pytest and bitbucket pipelines)
* Fluency in Python and Postgres
* Excellent problem-solving, communication, and collaboration skills
* Nice-to-have experience:
* + Proficiency with AI Coding Tools (e.g. Cursor/Claude Code)
  + Scaling software at a manufacturing startup
  + Molecular biology background
  + Experience with React

  

**What We Offer:**

* Competitive salary and equity.
* Generous benefits package including health, dental, and vision.
* Ongoing professional development and training opportunities.
* A collaborative and innovative work environment.
* The opportunity to be part of a company at the forefront of synthetic biology and innovation.

  

San Francisco Bay Area Pay Range

**$135,000 - $190,000 depending upon experience**

  

**Ansa Biotechnologies is an Equal Opportunity Employer.**

All applicants will be considered for employment without attention to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, veteran or disability status.

At Ansa, we’re building a community of intelligent and passionate humans that will help us change biotechnology research with our enzymatic DNA synthesis technology. We believe that challenging and trusting one another, and continuously learning are essential to our success. We believe that building diverse, inclusive and psychologically safe spaces are essential to a community culture that yields the happiest colleagues and friends, and the highest quality research.

As we are growing rapidly, this is an ever present goal: hiring the best people while building diversity in thought, experience and background within our team. jobs.title: Software Engineer - Product

**About Us**
------------

We are a well-funded, early-stage AI research and product lab focused on building the next generation of frontier multimodal AI models. Founded by former DeepMind researchers—including Andrew Dai, previously an engineering leader on Gemini—our mission is to push the frontier of visual and multimodal intelligence. Our first model, Glimpse, launched publicly in October 2026.

Our team currently consists of 25 world-class scientists and engineers. We raised a $55M seed round led by Altimeter Capital, Menlo Ventures, Striker VC, and NVIDIA. We are tackling foundational problems in artificial intelligence and translating cutting-edge multimodal research into scalable, real-world systems.

------------------

We are seeking a Software Engineer to lead the client-facing product for Glimpse. In this role, you will design and build the integration layer, including but not limited to API, web interfaces, and platform tools that external developers will use to interact with our multimodal models. You will also collaborate directly with research, infrastructure, and GTM teams to ensure smooth delivery of future model releases.

jobs.title: Software Development Engineer - AWS OpenSearch, OpenSearch Platform Team
jobs.description:
**DESCRIPTION**
---------------

Amazon OpenSearch Service powers search, log analytics, observability, and vector workloads for tens of thousands of customers. Every one of those customers runs on software that our Data Plane Platform team ships, and keeping it current means updating and managing software updates across millions of instances at scale, safely and continuously. We own the release engine for the managed OpenSearch data plane: the pipelines, the automation, and the Release Rover platform that take an upstream open source cut all the way to GA across every supported version and region.  
  
We are looking for a Software Development Engineer to help us turn releasing OpenSearch from a hand-coordinated effort into a fully automated, self-service platform. The team has already sharply reduced release cycle time, increased release throughput, consolidated its pipelines, and driven per-engineer release effort close to zero. You will build pieces of that system: the tooling, orchestration, and AI-assisted automation that let teams release safely with less manual effort.  
  
This is a hands-on builder role at the intersection of distributed systems, CI/CD, and developer experience, with a strong and growing emphasis on AI. You will own well-scoped components end to end, from design through operations, with mentorship from senior engineers on the team, and you will have real opportunity to apply AI and agentic automation to real release problems. The code you ship becomes part of the paved road the OpenSearch organization releases on.  
  
Key job responsibilities  
Build and operate the services, pipelines, and automation that update and manage software updates across millions of instances at scale, safely and continuously, across many versions and regions.  
Build and extend the self-service release platform so builders across the organization can ship features quickly and reliably.  
Improve release safety with staged rollouts, automated validation, rollback, and blast-radius controls so a bad change does not reach customers at scale.  
Apply AI and agentic automation to the parts of releasing that still require manual effort today.  
Own the operations of what you build: on-call, runbooks, metrics, and reducing operational load over time.  
Partner with the engineering teams who build and release on top of your platform.  
  
A day in the life  
You will split your time between building and operating the release platform. On the build side, you design and ship components that make releasing OpenSearch more automated and safer, and a large and growing part of that is applying AI and agentic automation to the parts of releasing that still take manual effort today. This is a team that treats AI as a core engineering tool, not an afterthought, so you will have real room to prototype, measure, and productionize AI-driven improvements to the release workflow. On the operational side, you keep active release trains healthy, support the teams releasing through the platform, and review changes with a focus on release safety. You will work closely with senior engineers who will help you grow your scope and design judgment over time.

jobs.description:
**Infrastructure Engineer**
---------------------------

**MSP4, LLC | Full-Time | Onsite (United States, posted location) | Up to 10% Regional Travel | 4 to 6 Years Experience | Reports To: Service Desk Manager, with technical escalation to the Senior Infrastructure Engineer**

### **About the Role**

MSP4 operates as the embedded IT department for a portfolio of clients spanning professional services, legal, distribution, manufacturing, and government sectors. Environments range from 50 to 1,500 users, with CMMC L2, NIST 800-171, and SOC 2 as active requirements.

This role keeps running environments running. You own the server and platform layer in steady state: the escalations that pass above the endpoint and site tier, the patching and monitoring and health work that stops incidents from happening, and the day-to-day administration of Windows Server, virtualization, storage, backup, and Microsoft cloud across your assigned clients.

You are the technical ceiling of the support organization. L2 escalations land with you and stop there unless the answer is a design change — at which point they go to the Senior Infrastructure Engineer who owns that domain. Knowing which is which, and saying so rather than guessing, is most of the job.

This is an onsite role at a client facility in your posted location, with regional coverage for nearby MSP4 clients. You are in the environment every day, and that presence is the reason the role exists.

**Infrastructure Engineer is a single tier with two specializations, Operations and Projects, sharing one compensation band and one core qualification set.** If build and migration work fits you better, say so on your cover page.

### **What You Will Do**

* Own L2 escalations at the server and platform layer: take what passes the endpoint and site tier, resolve it within scope, and escalate cleanly to the Senior Infrastructure Engineer when the fix is a design change rather than a repair
* Administer Windows Server environments day to day: Active Directory, DNS, DHCP, Group Policy, PKI, certificate services, and file and print services
* Operate Hyper-V and VMware vSphere clusters: VM lifecycle, capacity monitoring, host patching, live migration, HA behavior, and snapshot hygiene
* Run storage and clustering operations: provisioning, volume changes, capacity monitoring, and health checks against failover clustering and Storage Spaces Direct or comparable SAN/HCI platforms. Storage architecture sits with Senior Infrastructure Engineering
* Operate Veeam Backup and Replication: job management, backup verification, restore execution, repository and retention operations, and backup gap remediation
* Administer Microsoft 365 and Azure tenants: identity, licensing, Intune policy application, and Conditional Access within established standards
* Perform SQL Server platform work supporting client ERP and line-of-business applications: patching, version upgrades, backup coordination with Veeam, and baseline instance administration. DBA-level query tuning, indexing strategy, and application-side schema work sit with client DBAs or application vendors
* Execute network change at defined scope: firewall rule adds and modifications against approved standards, VLAN configuration, and switch port and access layer work. Routing, firewall policy design, and segmentation architecture sit with Senior Network Security Engineering — the stop-and-escalate boundary is stated, not guessed
* Apply STIG hardening and NIST 800-171 control execution at the server and platform layer in support of CMMC L2 and SOC 2, and capture the evidence
* Run the proactive work: patching cadence, monitoring coverage, health checks, capacity review, and closing the gap between a well-designed environment and a well-run one
* Receive completed projects into managed operations: review the handover, confirm the runbooks work, and own the platform from that point forward
* Communicate with client technical contacts and non-technical stakeholders on infrastructure work, change windows, and incidents
* Maintain ticketing and change discipline in a PSA or ITSM platform (Jira Service Management preferred; HaloPSA, ConnectWise, Autotask, or ServiceNow transferable)

### **Growth Path**

This specialization is a full career position, not a waiting room. Engineers who want to move toward design ownership have two routes: across into the Projects specialization, which leads to senior domain ownership, or deeper into platform expertise within Operations. Both are supported, and movement between specializations does not require re-interviewing into the tier.

### **Qualifications Matrix**

Candidates are scored against these. Rows 1 to 12 are the Infrastructure Engineer core, shared with the Projects specialization. Rows 13 to 17 are specific to Operations. Categories: Technical, Functional, Consulting, Credentials.

--------------------------

At Lam, as a Product Engineer, you thrive in high-stakes, dynamic environment, driving product development at the forefront of the semiconductor equipment industry. Collaborating closely with customers and internal teams, you will provide real-time problem-solving to customer challenges and to enhance our products. Your passion for engaging with customers and innovative engineering drives progress in our industry, tackling the once unsolvable.

**What you’ll do**
------------------

Manages new product introduction and production support engineering for a specific product or group of products from inception of ideas to in-house qualification to supporting at the customer. Participates in design, process, test, reliability and manufacturing engineering to solve product issues and production problems. Develops and sustains process improvements to reduce production costs and increase yields.

  

Develops new or modified hardware designs for electrostatic chucks (ESC’s) and supporting hardware in Lam plasma etchers. ESC’s are a highly multidisciplinary technology and offers opportunity to innovate on the intersection of physics, materials, and software algorithms to provide our customers differentiated solutions. Reviews process and customer requirements to define engineering specifications for ESC’s and ESC subsystems. Defines testing requirements for production-readiness qualification, reviews and defines process of record (POR) at parts suppliers, assesses suitability of materials used in production, and supports field issues related to this hardware. Part of an innovation process to develop novel solutions to one of the most challenging areas of an etch chamber. Handles full ESC life cycle from development, through product release and field support. Coordinates design reviews, risk assessments, and POR reviews with Lam engineering personnel to ensure successful product release and follow Lam product design business processes. Compiles and evaluates test data to determine appropriate hardware limitations and assesses risk of field failure according to customer process conditions.

  

Lam etch customers continue to tighten requirements on defectivity, process window, and uniformity, to meet the needs of ever shrinking device dimensions. Electrostatic chucks are at the forefront of these needs, as thermal uniformity, voltage process window, and to a large extent, defectivity limits are defined by this piece of hardware. Lam is continually improving ESC performance in all of these areas to meet customer needs. Understanding performance of this particular part of Lam plasma etchers requires a multidisciplinary background, incorporating elements of materials science, physics, mechanical and electrical engineering, to fully understand the implications of design changes on customer processing.

  

Senior engineers in this role are leading a small team of engineers and lab personnel to coordinate multiple subsystems to deliver the wafer requirements required of the next generation of hardware.

* Experience designing, specifying, building, operating and maintaining capital equipment test apparatus.

* Fundamental understanding of heat transfer, mass transfer, vacuum pressure and flow, thermodynamics and basic mechanics of materials

**Position Summary:**

We have an exciting opportunity to join our team as a Data Science Analyst/Engineer.
  
  
The Tan Lab at NYU is recruiting a Data Science Analyst/Engineer to develop and maintain computational infrastructure for machine learning in genomics. Our mission is to understand how elements of our genome regulate gene expression and its implications for human diseases. We combine machine learning, biological mechanisms, and large-scale data to understand how regulatory elements control transcription factors, 3D genome organization, and transcription. This position will maintain the lab's data and ML infrastructure, including processing, organizing, and managing terabyte-scale datasets; designing robust bioinformatics pipelines; and optimizing ML training pipelines and model architectures to accelerate and scale genomics research in the lab.

* Performs other duties as assigned.
* Independently design, execute, and communicate computational research projects in machine learning and functional genomics that advance the labs research mission.

* Develop and validate pipelines for assays such as RNA-seq, ATAC-seq, ChIP-seq, CUT&RUN/CUT&Tag, Hi-C, Micro-C, single-cell sequencing, and related emerging technologies.

* Develop new bioinformatics pipelines and work with wet-lab people to support new molecular assays or improve processing of current assays.

Good grasp of soware engineering principles. Experience in integrating modern

**DESCRIPTION**
---------------

The Creative X team within Amazon Advertising builds AI systems that understand and evaluate ad images and videos, so advertisers of every size can deliver high-quality experiences to customers. In this role, you will build image and video models that recognize what a creative contains, check whether it meets quality and brand requirements, and measure its effectiveness with measurable precision and recall.  
  
We invest in computer vision, video understanding, vision-language models (VLMs), multimodal representation learning, and evaluation science, including calibrating automated judges against human judgment. A central challenge is making these models work at scale: you will use techniques such as model distillation so that image and video understanding can run across billions of ad impressions. You will join a team of applied scientists, product managers and software developers, own science components from prototype to production, ship advertiser-facing features, and contribute to publications.  
  
Key job responsibilities  

* Build and improve image and video understanding models that extract semantic metadata from ad creatives, such as objects, products, scenes, text overlays, logos and brand elements, and shot-level events in video.

* Calibrate automated image and video judges against human annotations, using preference learning and active learning to raise agreement with expert reviewers.
* Run experiments, analyze the results, and turn findings into production improvements together with engineering and product partners. Share results in design reviews, documents and research publications.

The Creative X team within Amazon Advertising is on a mission to democratize access to high-quality ad creatives for advertisers worldwide. jobs.title: Software Engineer, Production Engineering, FinOps
jobs.description:
**About Ramp**
==============

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

Production Engineering is Ramp's infrastructure ownership layer. We exist to make Ramp faster, more reliable, and more scalable — and we do that by being embedded in the problems, not adjacent to them.

A few things that define how we operate:

* **One team, one company, one objective.** There is no "infra team" and "product team" — there is Ramp. We share the company's goals as our own. When a product team struggles with reliability or scalability, that is our struggle.
* **If reliability or scalability is at risk, we own it.** We don't wait to be invited, and we don't ask whose code it is. If a system is slow, if it breaks, if it won't scale — that's ours to lead, regardless of where it lives in the stack.
* **We go first, and we go fast.** When the path isn't obvious, we don't wait for someone else to find it. We move with urgency, propose the solution, align the stakeholders, and stay in until it's done — not until our ticket is closed.
* **We lead the way.** We find the next problem before it finds us. And when we solve it, we don't just fix it for ourselves — the patterns and standards we establish become the foundation the rest of Ramp builds on. That's not a side effect of the job; it's the job.
* **We stay calibrated.** Speed means nothing if we're moving in the wrong direction. We regularly stop and ask honestly whether what we're working on is still the highest-leverage thing we could be doing — the discipline that makes sure our effort compounds toward what actually matters.

**You cannot build the future of finance on shaky infrastructure.**

**Our Teams**
-------------

Production Engineering is organized into teams — but we think about teams differently. Teams are mutable. We build them around what needs to be done, not around what we need to do given the teams we already have. The structure below reflects our current priorities; it will evolve as Ramp does.

Right now, we operate across five areas:

* **Compute** — the foundation for running Ramp’s services and financial workflows: container orchestration, networking, load balancing, edge infrastructure, and asynchronous execution and messaging systems, including Temporal. The team owns production runtime reliability, scaling, isolation, and safe rollouts.
* **Storage** — the production data foundations that underpin Ramp: databases, caching, and object storage, with ownership of reliability, performance, capacity, recovery, and safe data movement.
* **Developer Infrastructure** — the shared infrastructure that helps engineers ship and understand production: CI/CD systems, observability foundations for logs, metrics, and traces, and visibility into infrastructure usage and cost.
* **Compliance Platform** — the infrastructure and operational capabilities for Ramp’s government environments and compliance needs: secure access, deployment paths, environment validation, and technical controls that let product teams deliver reliably within regulatory and compliance requirements.
* **Reliability Platform** — the tools and operating model for understanding and improving customer-facing reliability and performance: SLA/SLO measurement and reporting, customer-health visibility, monitoring and paging, and incident response and follow-through. The team helps product teams remain accountable for the health of what they build.

**What You'll Do**
------------------

As a FinOps Specialist within Production Engineering, you’ll help Ramp make better decisions about infrastructure spend – from resource usage and cloud commitments to vendor contracts and new investments.

You’ll work closely with Production Engineering leadership, Developer Infrastructure, Finance, Procurement, and engineering teams across Ramp. You’ll bring financial depth, investigate opportunities independently, and partner with engineers to turn recommendations into measurable results.

This is a senior individual contributor role.

Day to day, you will:

* **Set direction for infrastructure cost management.** Identify the highest-impact opportunities across Ramp, establish priorities with Production Engineering leadership and partner teams, and build a roadmap that balances immediate savings with lasting improvements.
* **Understand and explain our spend.** Investigate costs across AWS, observability, and AI providers. Connect changes to usage, architecture, customer growth, and engineering decisions, and help teams distinguish expected investment from avoidable waste.
* **Embed with teams early.** Partner with product and infrastructure teams during design and planning. Help them evaluate cost implications, model how systems will scale, and make informed tradeoffs before committing to an architecture or vendor.
* **Build forecasts we can defend.** Work with engineers to understand upcoming launches, migrations, and capacity needs. Translate those plans into financial models that explain expected spend, key assumptions, and uncertainty.
* **Shape commitment and vendor strategy.** Model cloud discounts, commitment levels, pay

**DESCRIPTION**
---------------

AWS Specialist Technology Team (STT) is seeking a Software Development Engineer to join the Specialist AI Tooling engineering team - the group building AI-native, agentic solutions that are fundamentally transforming how thousands of AWS technical specialists and field team members develop expertise, get matched to customer engagements, and how AWS service teams consume customer feedback at scale. If you want to build production agentic AI systems that impact thousands of users daily - not research prototypes, but real AI agents solving real problems - this is the role for you.  
  
You will design, build, and operate core components across four interconnected products that collectively power the intelligence layer of AWS's specialist ecosystem:  
  
AWS Learning Agent - A new generative AI-powered, agentic learning system that replaces static training paths with personalized, cross-domain skill development for every builder in the AWS technical field. Powered by a structured skill graph, persistent learner profiles, and the Specialist Knowledge Vault, the Learning Agent delivers adaptive learning journeys via a custom console, in Kiro, Claude, Quick and wherever builders work.  
Intelligent Routing Agent - A new AI-driven routing engine that matches 136K+ annual specialist requests to verified domain experts using validated skill profiles rather than manually maintained lists - reducing resolution time (currently 7.72 days) and enabling precision matching at scale.  
Technical Field Community (TFC) Hub - The platform powering 46 Technical Field Communities, managing member engagement, competency tracking, learning path orchestration, and community-driven content curation across AWS's specialist network.  
Service 360 - A GenAI summarization and prioritization engine that aggregates customer feedback signals (PFRs, SpecReqs, SFDC Opportunity data) into categorized, prioritized service recommendations - automating what was previously a manual closed-loop feedback process to influence the roadmap for AWS public service teams.  
  
This is a high-impact, AI-first engineering role where you will build agentic systems, ship production GenAI features, and solve hard problems at the intersection of knowledge graphs, multi-agent orchestration, LLM-powered personalization, and retrieval-augmented generation - all at AWS scale, using the very AI services AWS builds for its customers.

Design and build scalable distributed systems and APIs that power the TFC Hub platform, serving thousands of community members across 46 technical domains.  
Drive operational excellence for production services - owning CI/CD, monitoring, alarming, on-call, and incident response for systems serving thousands of daily users.  
Contribute to technical strategy and architecture decisions, proactively identifying opportunities to improve system performance, reliability, and developer velocity.

You will be joining a high-growth engineering organization that is at the forefront of applying generative AI and agentic technologies to transform how AWS field teams operate. The pace of innovation is high, the problems are ambiguous, and the impact is measured across thousands of field team members and the customers they serve. This role offers the opportunity to shape how teams consume and act on AI-powered tools - building systems from the ground up that define the future of specialist expertise at AWS.

Build agentic AI systems

Cross-cutting  
  
Collaborate with Finance, Accounting, and Tax stakeholders to translate business requirements into AI-driven solutions  
Own production systems end-to-end, from deployment and monitoring to incident response and iterative improvement  
Raise the team's bar through code reviews, docs, mentoring, and promoting AI-assisted development

This is a hands-on engineering role where you'll work on SAP-side development (ABAP, CDS, RAP, OData) and AWS-native engineering (Lambda, Step Functions, MCP servers, Bedrock, CDK) — owning integrations end-to-end.

new_jobs.description:
**Location**

San Francisco

**Employment Type**

Research & Engineering

Overview

**Role:** Member of Technical Staff - GPU Inference Engineer
  
**Team:** Research & Engineering
  
**Location:** San Francisco; Boston; Remote
  
**Location Type:** Hybrid
  
**Employment Type:** Full-time

**About Liquid AI**
-------------------

Spun out of MIT CSAIL, we build general-purpose AI systems that run efficiently across deployment targets, from data center accelerators to on-device hardware, ensuring low latency, minimal memory usage, privacy, and reliability. We partner with enterprises across consumer electronics, automotive, life sciences, and financial services. We are scaling rapidly and need exceptional people to help us get there.

**The Opportunity**
-------------------

GPU inference sits underneath much of how we build and ship models at Liquid. Evaluation runs, synthetic data generation, and our API service all depend on how fast and how cheaply we can serve Liquid Foundation Models on GPUs, and demand for that work is growing. You will join the small team that owns our GPU serving stack, built on vLLM and SGLang, and make it faster and cheaper to run.

This is a high-ownership role: you will be pointed at whichever inference bottleneck matters most and carry it from profiling to a benchmarked result. The work sits at the serving-framework level rather than in custom CUDA kernels, which is a separate role on the team.

**What We're Looking For**
--------------------------

We need someone who:

* **Reasons from first principles:** Explains why a workload is slow before changing it, working from what the model and the GPU are actually doing rather than from framework defaults.
* **Picks up the next problem and owns it:** Moves from evaluation throughput to data generation to API serving as priorities shift, and takes each one through to a measured result.
* **Makes other teams faster:** Works directly with the researchers and engineers who depend on inference, and treats their throughput as the result that counts.

**The Work**
------------

* Own and improve our GPU serving stack on vLLM and SGLang, from configuration and scheduling choices to changes in the frameworks themselves
* Speed up large-scale evaluation and synthetic data generation, and design the inference pipelines those workloads run on
* Select, profile, and benchmark the inference engine behind our API service, and adapt the API layer around it
* Integrate Liquid Foundation Models into vLLM, SGLang, and Hugging Face Transformers, and maintain those public integrations as models and frameworks change
* Diagnose throughput and latency problems alongside the researchers and serving engineers who hit them

**Experience & Capabilities**
-----------------------------

**What you'll need:**

* Hands-on experience running LLM inference on GPUs with a serving framework such as vLLM or SGLang, beyond default configuration
* First-principles understanding of LLM inference: the transformer forward pass, autoregressive decoding on a GPU, and the latency, throughput, and memory trade-offs that follow
* Solid grasp of GPU fundamentals as they bear on inference. You do not need to have written CUDA kernels
* Experience profiling and benchmarking inference workloads and acting on what the numbers show
* Strong Python and PyTorch, and comfort reading and changing large open-source codebases

**Helpful, not required:**

* Merged contributions to vLLM, SGLang, or FlashInfer
* Lower-level GPU optimization experience, such as CUDA or Triton kernels
* Experience building high-throughput batch inference for evaluation or synthetic data generation

**What Success Looks Like (Year One)**
--------------------------------------

* Evaluation and synthetic data generation run measurably faster and at lower cost per token on the same hardware, freeing GPU capacity for other work
* The inference engine and configuration behind our API service are chosen on benchmark evidence, and have been profiled and tuned for latency and throughput
* Liquid models run correctly and efficiently in the public serving frameworks and libraries our users rely on, including vLLM, SGLang, and Transformers

**What We Offer**
-----------------

* **Problems standard stacks don't solve:** Our hybrid architectures do not drop into off-the-shelf serving frameworks unchanged, and the inference you speed up feeds how every Liquid model is evaluated and trained. High ownership from day one. [INFERRED - review this line]
* **Compensation & Equity:** Competitive base salary plus equity, so you share in what we build. Final offers reflect skills, experience, and location.
* **Time Off:** Unlimited PTO, plus company-wide Refill Days, long weekends when the whole company rests together.
* **Health & Wellbeing:** Comprehensive health coverage, with details varying by location.
* **Paid Leave:** Paid leave for pregnancy, parenting, medical needs, and caring for family.

new_jobs.title: Robotics Research Engineer (VLA Engineer)
new_jobs.description:
**About Trener**

Trener is a Physical AI company building software-defined robotics for industrial automation. Our platform is built on the ROS 2 ecosystem, and our product, Acteris, is running in production with real customers on real factory floors — not in a demo lab.

Backed by a $32M Series A, we operate from dual headquarters in San Jose, California and Trondheim, Norway, with teammates across six countries. We work by four values: Move Fast Together, Earn Customer Champions, Deliver with Excellence, and Challenge the Possible.  
  
**The role**

You will turn VLA research into robot behavior that works on a production line. Industrial work cells are high-mix and unforgiving: parts vary, lighting changes, and a policy that succeeds 80% of the time in simulation is not a product.

As a Robotics Research Engineer in T-Labs, you will own the full loop — data, training, evaluation, and on-robot deployment — for foundation-model-based manipulation policies. You will work alongside our AI compute, perception, and integration engineers to move models from paper to pilot to customer deployment.  
  
**What you’ll do**

* Design, train, and fine-tune Vision-Language-Action models for industrial manipulation tasks such as pick-and-place, kitting, machine tending, and assembly.
* Build and scale robot learning data pipelines: teleoperation and demonstration collection, data curation, augmentation, and synthetic data from simulation.
* Adapt pretrained vision-language backbones to robot action spaces, including action tokenization, diffusion or flow-matching action heads, and multi-camera inputs.
* Define evaluation protocols and benchmarks that measure real-world success rate, robustness, and generalization to new parts, cells, and instructions.
* Close the sim-to-real gap using simulation environments (Isaac Sim/Isaac Lab, MuJoCo, or Gazebo) and domain randomization.
* Deploy policies on physical robots through ROS 2, working with the AI Compute team to meet latency and memory targets on edge hardware (quantization, distillation, TensorRT).
* Track and reproduce state-of-the-art research, and share findings through internal tech talks, write-ups, and — where appropriate — publications at venues such as CoRL, RSS, ICRA, and IROS.
* Partner with Product, Integration, and customer-facing teams to turn customer use cases into learnable tasks and measurable milestones.

**What you’ll bring**

* MS or PhD in Robotics, Computer Science, Electrical/Mechanical Engineering, or a related field — or equivalent industry experience.
* 3+ years of hands-on experience in robot learning, imitation learning, or reinforcement learning applied to manipulation.
* Direct experience training or fine-tuning large multimodal models (VLMs, VLAs, or transformer-based policies) in PyTorch or JAX.
* Strong Python skills and working proficiency in C++.
* Experience running learned policies on physical robot hardware, not only in simulation.
* Familiarity with ROS or ROS 2.
* Comfort with distributed GPU training and experiment tracking (e.g., Weights & Biases, MLflow).
* A track record of shipping research into working systems, and clear communication across research and engineering teams.

**Nice to have**

* Publications at CoRL, RSS, ICRA, IROS, NeurIPS, ICML, or CVPR on robot learning or embodied AI.
* Contributions to open-source robot learning projects.
* Experience with diffusion policies, flow matching, or world models for control.
* Hands-on work with industrial arms (e.g., UR, ABB, KUKA, FANUC) and grippers, force/torque sensing, or tactile sensing.
* Experience optimizing models for edge inference (quantization, pruning, distillation, TensorRT, NVIDIA Jetson).
* Background in large-scale teleoperation or data collection infrastructure.
* Experience at a robotics startup or in a production manufacturing environment.

Build agentic AI systems

Manage infrastructure with CDK, including CI/CD, IAM, VPC connectivity, secrets management, and beta/gamma/prod environments

Set up monitoring for agents and services (CloudWatch metrics, logs, alarms, tracing)  
  
Cross-cutting  
  
Collaborate with Finance, Accounting, and Tax stakeholders to translate business requirements into AI-driven solutions  
Own production systems end-to-end, from deployment and monitoring to incident response and iterative improvement  
Raise the team's bar through code reviews, docs, mentoring, and promoting AI-assisted development

You might be a backend or full-stack engineer who wants to work more closely with customers, or an infrastructure engineer with deep experience in cloud systems, Kubernetes, and networking. new_jobs.title: Software Development Engineer - AWS OpenSearch, OpenSearch Platform Team
new_jobs.description:
**DESCRIPTION**
---------------

Amazon OpenSearch Service powers search, log analytics, observability, and vector workloads for tens of thousands of customers. Every one of those customers runs on software that our Data Plane Platform team ships, and keeping it current means updating and managing software updates across millions of instances at scale, safely and continuously. We own the release engine for the managed OpenSearch data plane: the pipelines, the automation, and the Release Rover platform that take an upstream open source cut all the way to GA across every supported version and region.  
  
We are looking for a Software Development Engineer to help us turn releasing OpenSearch from a hand-coordinated effort into a fully automated, self-service platform. The team has already sharply reduced release cycle time, increased release throughput, consolidated its pipelines, and driven per-engineer release effort close to zero. You will build pieces of that system: the tooling, orchestration, and AI-assisted automation that let teams release safely with less manual effort.  
  
This is a hands-on builder role at the intersection of distributed systems, CI/CD, and developer experience, with a strong and growing emphasis on AI. You will own well-scoped components end to end, from design through operations, with mentorship from senior engineers on the team, and you will have real opportunity to apply AI and agentic automation to real release problems. The code you ship becomes part of the paved road the OpenSearch organization releases on.  
  
Key job responsibilities  
Build and operate the services, pipelines, and automation that update and manage software updates across millions of instances at scale, safely and continuously, across many versions and regions.  
Build and extend the self-service release platform so builders across the organization can ship features quickly and reliably.  
Improve release safety with staged rollouts, automated validation, rollback, and blast-radius controls so a bad change does not reach customers at scale.  
Apply AI and agentic automation to the parts of releasing that still require manual effort today.  
Own the operations of what you build: on-call, runbooks, metrics, and reducing operational load over time.  
Partner with the engineering teams who build and release on top of your platform.  
  
A day in the life  
You will split your time between building and operating the release platform. On the build side, you design and ship components that make releasing OpenSearch more automated and safer, and a large and growing part of that is applying AI and agentic automation to the parts of releasing that still take manual effort today. This is a team that treats AI as a core engineering tool, not an afterthought, so you will have real room to prototype, measure, and productionize AI-driven improvements to the release workflow. On the operational side, you keep active release trains healthy, support the teams releasing through the platform, and review changes with a focus on release safety. You will work closely with senior engineers who will help you grow your scope and design judgment over time.

**BASIC QUALIFICATIONS**
