new_jobs.description:
**Infrastructure Engineer**
---------------------------

**MSP4, LLC | Full-Time | Onsite (United States, posted location) | Up to 10% Regional Travel | 4 to 6 Years Experience | Reports To: Service Desk Manager, with technical escalation to the Senior Infrastructure Engineer**

### **About the Role**

MSP4 operates as the embedded IT department for a portfolio of clients spanning professional services, legal, distribution, manufacturing, and government sectors. Environments range from 50 to 1,500 users, with CMMC L2, NIST 800-171, and SOC 2 as active requirements.

This role keeps running environments running. You own the server and platform layer in steady state: the escalations that pass above the endpoint and site tier, the patching and monitoring and health work that stops incidents from happening, and the day-to-day administration of Windows Server, virtualization, storage, backup, and Microsoft cloud across your assigned clients.

You are the technical ceiling of the support organization. L2 escalations land with you and stop there unless the answer is a design change — at which point they go to the Senior Infrastructure Engineer who owns that domain. Knowing which is which, and saying so rather than guessing, is most of the job.

This is an onsite role at a client facility in your posted location, with regional coverage for nearby MSP4 clients. You are in the environment every day, and that presence is the reason the role exists.

**Infrastructure Engineer is a single tier with two specializations, Operations and Projects, sharing one compensation band and one core qualification set.** If build and migration work fits you better, say so on your cover page.

### **What You Will Do**

* Own L2 escalations at the server and platform layer: take what passes the endpoint and site tier, resolve it within scope, and escalate cleanly to the Senior Infrastructure Engineer when the fix is a design change rather than a repair
* Administer Windows Server environments day to day: Active Directory, DNS, DHCP, Group Policy, PKI, certificate services, and file and print services
* Operate Hyper-V and VMware vSphere clusters: VM lifecycle, capacity monitoring, host patching, live migration, HA behavior, and snapshot hygiene
* Run storage and clustering operations: provisioning, volume changes, capacity monitoring, and health checks against failover clustering and Storage Spaces Direct or comparable SAN/HCI platforms. Storage architecture sits with Senior Infrastructure Engineering
* Operate Veeam Backup and Replication: job management, backup verification, restore execution, repository and retention operations, and backup gap remediation
* Administer Microsoft 365 and Azure tenants: identity, licensing, Intune policy application, and Conditional Access within established standards
* Perform SQL Server platform work supporting client ERP and line-of-business applications: patching, version upgrades, backup coordination with Veeam, and baseline instance administration. DBA-level query tuning, indexing strategy, and application-side schema work sit with client DBAs or application vendors
* Execute network change at defined scope: firewall rule adds and modifications against approved standards, VLAN configuration, and switch port and access layer work. Routing, firewall policy design, and segmentation architecture sit with Senior Network Security Engineering — the stop-and-escalate boundary is stated, not guessed
* Apply STIG hardening and NIST 800-171 control execution at the server and platform layer in support of CMMC L2 and SOC 2, and capture the evidence
* Run the proactive work: patching cadence, monitoring coverage, health checks, capacity review, and closing the gap between a well-designed environment and a well-run one
* Receive completed projects into managed operations: review the handover, confirm the runbooks work, and own the platform from that point forward
* Communicate with client technical contacts and non-technical stakeholders on infrastructure work, change windows, and incidents
* Maintain ticketing and change discipline in a PSA or ITSM platform (Jira Service Management preferred; HaloPSA, ConnectWise, Autotask, or ServiceNow transferable)

### **Growth Path**

This specialization is a full career position, not a waiting room. Engineers who want to move toward design ownership have two routes: across into the Projects specialization, which leads to senior domain ownership, or deeper into platform expertise within Operations. Both are supported, and movement between specializations does not require re-interviewing into the tier.

The Creative X team within Amazon Advertising builds AI systems that understand and evaluate ad images and videos, so advertisers of every size can deliver high-quality experiences to customers. In this role, you will build image and video models that recognize what a creative contains, check whether it meets quality and brand requirements, and measure its effectiveness with measurable precision and recall.  
  
We invest in computer vision, video understanding, vision-language models (VLMs), multimodal representation learning, and evaluation science, including calibrating automated judges against human judgment. A central challenge is making these models work at scale: you will use techniques such as model distillation so that image and video understanding can run across billions of ad impressions. You will join a team of applied scientists, product managers and software developers, own science components from prototype to production, ship advertiser-facing features, and contribute to publications.

new_jobs.title: Software Engineer, Production Engineering, FinOps
new_jobs.description:
**About Ramp**
==============

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

Production Engineering is Ramp's infrastructure ownership layer. We exist to make Ramp faster, more reliable, and more scalable — and we do that by being embedded in the problems, not adjacent to them.

A few things that define how we operate:

* **One team, one company, one objective.** There is no "infra team" and "product team" — there is Ramp. We share the company's goals as our own. When a product team struggles with reliability or scalability, that is our struggle.
* **If reliability or scalability is at risk, we own it.** We don't wait to be invited, and we don't ask whose code it is. If a system is slow, if it breaks, if it won't scale — that's ours to lead, regardless of where it lives in the stack.
* **We go first, and we go fast.** When the path isn't obvious, we don't wait for someone else to find it. We move with urgency, propose the solution, align the stakeholders, and stay in until it's done — not until our ticket is closed.
* **We lead the way.** We find the next problem before it finds us. And when we solve it, we don't just fix it for ourselves — the patterns and standards we establish become the foundation the rest of Ramp builds on. That's not a side effect of the job; it's the job.
* **We stay calibrated.** Speed means nothing if we're moving in the wrong direction. We regularly stop and ask honestly whether what we're working on is still the highest-leverage thing we could be doing — the discipline that makes sure our effort compounds toward what actually matters.

**You cannot build the future of finance on shaky infrastructure.**

**Our Teams**
-------------

Production Engineering is organized into teams — but we think about teams differently. Teams are mutable. We build them around what needs to be done, not around what we need to do given the teams we already have. The structure below reflects our current priorities; it will evolve as Ramp does.

Right now, we operate across five areas:

* **Compute** — the foundation for running Ramp’s services and financial workflows: container orchestration, networking, load balancing, edge infrastructure, and asynchronous execution and messaging systems, including Temporal. The team owns production runtime reliability, scaling, isolation, and safe rollouts.
